questions.question: There are two pipes A and B, each can fill the tank in 20 hours. Both pipes are opened together and due to leakage it was found that take 2 hours more to fill the tank. If the tank is full then in what time leakage will empty the tank.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by **Pipe A** and **Pipe B** together = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 hr.

Actual time taken to fill the **tank** with **leakage** = 10 + 2 = 12 hr.

Time to empty by **leakage** = (Initial Time × New Time) ÷ (Difference in Time)

⇒ (10 × 12) ÷ (12 − 10) = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time for **Pipe A** = 20 hr, **Pipe B** = 20 hr. Extra time due to **leakage** = 2 hr.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

First, calculate the time taken by A and B together without **leakage**:

⇒ Time (A + B) = (20 × 20) ÷ (20 + 20) = 400 ÷ 40 = 10 hr.

Now, time with **leakage** = 10 + 2 = 12 hr.

 
 

 **Source**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

⇒ Efficiency of **leakage** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of (A + B + Leak)

⇒ Efficiency of **leakage** = 6 − 5 = 1 unit/hr.

⇒ Time taken by **leakage** to empty the **tank** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Efficiency

In pipe and cistern problems, a **leakage** or an **outlet pipe** is always considered to have **negative efficiency** as it removes water from the tank.

Combined Efficiency Rule

If pipe X fills in 'x' hours and pipe Y empties in 'y' hours, the net work per hour is (1/x − 1/y). If the result is positive, the tank fills; if negative, it empties.

Time and Work Relation

Time is **inversely proportional** to efficiency. If efficiency is doubled, the time required to complete the same work is halved.</p

questions.question: Ravi & Raghav complete a certain work in 25 days. If both started working together & Ravi left after 15 days, then Raghav do the remaining work in 20 days. How many days Raghav will take to complete the same work alone?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let total work is 1 unit.

One day work of Ravi & Raghav = 1/25

15 days work of Ravi & Raghav = 15/25 = 3/5

Remaining work = 1 - 3/5 = 2/5 unit

Now, 2/5 of work by Raghav is completed in 20 days

1 unit work is completed in (5/2) × 20 = 50 days

**∴ Raghav will complete the work alone in 50 days.**

questions.question: The side of a square is 5 cm. How many times will the new area become, if the side of the square is doubled?

If the **side** of a square is increased by a factor of **n**, then the **area** increases by a factor of **n²**.

Here, the side is **doubled**, so **n = 2**.

New Area = **2²** × Original Area = **4** × Original Area.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Original Area = **5 × 5** = **25 cm²**

⇒ New Side = **2 × 5** = **10 cm**

⇒ New Area = **10 × 10** = **100 cm²**

⇒ Ratio = **New Area ÷ Original Area** = **100 ÷ 25** = **4**

**∴ The correct answer is 4 times.**

Perimeter Scaling

If the side of a square is doubled, the **perimeter** also gets **doubled** (scaled by **k**).

Volume Scaling

For 3D objects like cubes, if the side is doubled, the **volume** becomes **2³ = 8 times** the original.</p

questions.question: Find the value of cos 47° sec 133° + sin 44° cosec 136°.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert obtuse angles to supplementary forms: 133° = 180° − 47° and 136° = 180° − 44°.

Using 2ⁿd quadrant rules: sec(180° − θ) = −sec θ and cosec(180° − θ) = cosec θ.

Expression = cos 47° × (−sec 47°) + sin 44° × cosec 44°.

Since cos θ × sec θ = 1 and sin θ × cosec θ = 1:

Result = −1 + 1 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = cos 47° sec 133° + sin 44° cosec 136°

**Formula Used:**

sec(180° − θ) = −sec θ

cosec(180° − θ) = cosec θ

cos θ × sec θ = 1

sin θ × cosec θ = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Split the obtuse angles into (180° − θ) form to simplify.

⇒ sec 133° = sec(180° − 47°) = −sec 47°

⇒ cosec 136° = cosec(180° − 44°) = cosec 44°

⇒ Substitute these simplified values back into the given expression.

⇒ Expression = cos 47° × (−sec 47°) + sin 44° × cosec 44°

⇒ Expression = −(cos 47° × sec 47°) + (sin 44° × cosec 44°)

⇒ Since a trigonometric function multiplied by its reciprocal is exactly 1:

⇒ Expression = −1 + 1 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

ASTC Rule

In the 2ⁿd quadrant (90° to 180°), only Sine (sin) and Cosecant (cosec) are positive. Cosine (cos), Secant (sec), Tangent (tan), and Cotangent (cot) are negative.

Reciprocal Identities

sin θ × cosec θ = 1 | cos θ × sec θ = 1 | tan θ × cot θ = 1.

Supplementary Angles

Angles that add up to 180° are supplementary. sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, while cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.

questions.question: The annual incomes of Anand and Bharath are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5 and their annual expenses are in the ratio 1 ∶ 3. If each of them saves Rs. 10,000 at the end of the year, then the annual income of Bharath is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Incomes** (Anand : Bharath) = 3 : 5 (Difference = 2 units)

Ratio of **Expenses** (Anand : Bharath) = 1 : 3 (Difference = 2 units)

Since differences are equal, **Savings** = Income − Expense ⇒ (3 − 1) = (5 − 3) = 2 units.

Given 2 units = ₹10,000 → 1 unit = ₹5,000.

Annual Income of **Bharath** = 5 units = 5 × ₹5,000 = ₹25,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de6e2e0293cd04cfc879d9b2df7a9299090801a5bcd6579b949025c30ca8577e.png] 

**Given:** Ratio of incomes = 3 : 5 | Ratio of expenses = 1 : 3 | Savings = ₹10,000 each.

**Formula:** Income − Savings = Expenditure

⇒ Let annual incomes be 3x and 5x.

⇒ (3x − 10,000) / (5x − 10,000) = 1 / 3

⇒ 3 × (3x − 10,000) = 1 × (5x − 10,000)

⇒ 9x − 30,000 = 5x − 10,000

⇒ 4x = 20,000

⇒ x = 5,000

⇒ Bharath's Income = 5x = 5 × 5,000 = ₹25,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Relation

The fundamental equation for financial arithmetic is Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Ratio Balancing Method

If the difference between income and expense ratios is not equal for both parties, multiply the ratios by the difference of the other ratio to balance the units of savings.

Cross Multiplication Method

A quick way to solve ratio problems involving additions or subtractions: (Initial Ratio Product Difference) = (Product Difference of Change and Final Ratio).

questions.question: If the sum of lateral surface area and total surface area of the hemisphere is 770 cm², then find the difference of lateral surface area and total surface area of the hemisphere. (in cm²)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LSA of hemisphere = 2πr² and TSA of hemisphere = 3πr².

Sum = 2πr² + 3πr² = 5πr² = 770 cm².

Difference = 3πr² − 2πr² = πr².

Difference = 770 ÷ 5 = 154 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 154 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of **Lateral Surface Area (LSA)** and **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 770 cm².

**Formula Used:**

⇒ LSA of Hemisphere = 2πr²

⇒ TSA of Hemisphere = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcdfa251479b969fc7afe4b9379d2fc0cef874e355a7f6441534bea79c055752.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = LSA + TSA = 2πr² + 3πr²

⇒ 5πr² = 770

⇒ πr² = 770 ÷ 5

⇒ πr² = 154

⇒ Difference = TSA − LSA

⇒ Difference = 3πr² − 2πr² = πr²

⇒ Difference = 154 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 154 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Hemisphere

The volume of a hemisphere is exactly half the volume of a sphere: V = (2/3)πr³.

Sphere Surface Area

For a complete sphere, the surface area is 4πr². Note that a sphere has no distinct base area.

Base Area of Hemisphere

The flat circular face of a hemisphere has an area of πr², which accounts for the difference between TSA and LSA.</p

questions.question: Train ‘A’ requires 15 seconds to cross train ‘B’ of length 300 m moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 36 km/h. Further, train ‘A’ requires 30 seconds to cross a 500 m long stationary train ‘C’. Find the length (in m) of train ‘A’.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of train B = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

For Train A to cross Train B, relative speed = Speed to cross stationary C + Speed of B.

⇒ (LA + 300) ÷ 15 = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 + 10

⇒ 2LA + 600 = LA + 500 + 300

⇒ LA = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train B = 300 m

Speed of train B = 36 km/h = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

Length of stationary train C = 500 m

Time to cross B = 15 s, Time to cross C = 30 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = VA + VB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/769276248a78aa7449ab538025ee5c0e35cc38fac6df147a92bbfaa750d86c87.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of train A be LA and its speed be VA.

⇒ Time taken to cross train B = (LA + 300) ÷ (VA + 10) = 15

⇒ VA + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15 --- (1)

⇒ Time taken to cross stationary train C = (LA + 500) ÷ VA = 30

⇒ VA = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 --- (2)

⇒ Substituting equation (2) into equation (1):

⇒ [(LA + 500) ÷ 30] + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15

⇒ Multiplying by 30 on both sides:

⇒ LA + 500 + 300 = 2 × (LA + 300)

⇒ LA + 800 = 2LA + 600

⇒ LA = 800 − 600 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂). For the same direction, it is the difference (V₁ − V₂).

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses an object with length (like a platform or another train), the total distance covered equals the sum of lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

questions.question: In a mixture alcohol and water are in the ratio of 3 ∶ 7. If it contains 4 litres more water than alcohol, then what will be the quantity of water in mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of **Alcohol** : **Water** = 3 : 7

Difference in **ratio** = 7 − 3 = 4 units

According to the question, 4 units = 4 **litres** ⇒ 1 unit = 1 litre

Quantity of **Water** = 7 units = 7 × 1 = 7 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 7 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given **Ratio** of **Alcohol** and **Water** = 3 : 7

Difference in quantity = 4 **litres**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/859aefa2a058629b2f085aebec0bde03a6ed232b89f5fac80d75869590beaea0.png] 

Let the quantity of **Alcohol** and **Water** be 3x and 7x respectively.

⇒ **Water** − **Alcohol** = 4

⇒ 7x − 3x = 4

⇒ 4x = 4

⇒ x = 1

⇒ Quantity of **Water** = 7x = 7 × 1 = 7 **litres**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Difference Rule

If two quantities are in the ratio a : b and their difference is 'D', then the value of 1 part = D ÷ (b − a).

Total Mixture Quantity

The total quantity of the mixture is calculated by (a + b) × value of 1 part. In this case, (3 + 7) × 1 = 10 litres.

Percentage Composition

Percentage of a component in a mixture = [Component Part ÷ Total Parts] × 100. For water, it is (7 ÷ 10) × 100 = 70%.</p

questions.question: If the simple interest on a sum of money for two years at 5% per annum is Rs.50, then what is the compound interest when compounding annually at the same rate and for the same time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of **Simple Interest** for 2 years = 5% + 5% = 10%

Effective rate of **Compound Interest** for 2 years = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = 10.25%

Given, 10% corresponds to ₹50

Value of 10.25% = (50 ÷ 10) × 10.25 = 5 × 10.25 = ₹51.25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹51.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Simple Interest (SI) = ₹50, Time (T) = 2 years, Rate (R) = 5% per annum.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50a75b25eb945fcea9127639a8b2079269471bc4ccc5ed46df8a9a84bc7ed76d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Principal (P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (50 × 100) ÷ (5 × 2)

⇒ P = 5000 ÷ 10 = ₹500

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = 500 × [(1 + 5/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI = 500 × [(1.05)² − 1]

⇒ CI = 500 × [1.1025 − 1]

⇒ CI = 500 × 0.1025 = ₹51.25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹51.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference is given by the formula: CI − SI = P(R/100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference is given by the formula: CI − SI = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate r% compounded annually for 2 years, the effective rate is r + r + (r²/100)%.

questions.question: In rhombus ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD intersects at the point O. If ∠CDO = 50∘, then find the ∠DAB.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **rhombus**, the diagonals **bisect** the interior angles of the vertices.

Given ∠CDO = 50°, the total angle at vertex D is ∠ADC = 2 × ∠CDO = 2 × 50° = 100°.

In a rhombus, **adjacent angles** are supplementary (sum = 180°).

∠DAB + ∠ADC = 180°

∠DAB = 180° − 100° = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠CDO = 50° in **Rhombus** ABCD where **diagonals** AC and BD intersect at O.

**Property Used:** Diagonals of a rhombus are **perpendicular** to each other and **bisect** the internal angles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5c14474bfc034649e2f956a495bebccdef268c3baac06a21c651839a8c31d50.png] 

⇒ In ΔCDO, ∠COD = 90° (Diagonals are perpendicular)

⇒ ∠CDO = 50° (Given)

⇒ In ΔCDO: ∠DCO = 180° − (90° + 50°) = 40°

⇒ Since diagonal AC **bisects** ∠BCD, ∠BCD = 2 × ∠DCO

⇒ ∠BCD = 2 × 40° = 80°

⇒ In a rhombus, **opposite angles** are equal: ∠DAB = ∠BCD

⇒ ∠DAB = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are equal, and opposite sides are parallel. Diagonals bisect each other at 90°.

Angle Bisector Property

Each diagonal of a rhombus bisects the interior angles of the vertices it joins.

Area of a Rhombus

The area can be calculated using the diagonals: Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂.

Consecutive Angles

Any two adjacent (consecutive) angles in a rhombus are supplementary, meaning they sum to 180°.

questions.question: Length of rectangular field is 3 times its breadth, if area of the field is 432 m². Find the cost of fencing it at Rs. 2 per metre.

questions.question: A man travels 100 km at 50 km/h, the next 120 km at 40 km/h and the next 150 km at 60 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Distance** = 100 + 120 + 150 = 370 km

**Total Time** = (100 ÷ 50) + (120 ÷ 40) + (150 ÷ 60) = 2 + 3 + 2.5 = 7.5 hours

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 370 ÷ 7.5 = 740 ÷ 15 = 148 ÷ 3 = 49(1/3) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 49(1/3) km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First segment: **Distance** (d₁) = 100 km, **Speed** (s₁) = 50 km/h

Second segment: **Distance** (d₂) = 120 km, **Speed** (s₂) = 40 km/h

Third segment: **Distance** (d₃) = 150 km, **Speed** (s₃) = 60 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b1bff0f8b7a36c3537c054e1cd59de40ff2447f37ff6315c6596a8f80825ea4.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

**Time** = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Time taken for 1st part (t₁)** = 100 ÷ 50 = 2 hours

⇒ **Time taken for 2ⁿd part (t₂)** = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours

⇒ **Time taken for 3rd part (t₃)** = 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours

⇒ **Total Time** = 2 + 3 + 2.5 = 7.5 hours

⇒ **Total Distance** = 100 + 120 + 150 = 370 km

⇒ **Average Speed** = 370 ÷ 7.5

⇒ **Average Speed** = 370 ÷ (15 ÷ 2) = (370 × 2) ÷ 15

⇒ **Average Speed** = 740 ÷ 15 = 148 ÷ 3

⇒ **Average Speed** = 49(1/3) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 49(1/3) km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

The average speed for any journey is always calculated as the **Total Distance** covered divided by the **Total Time** taken.

Equal Distance Shortcut

If a body travels two equal distances at speeds **x** and **y**, the average speed is given by (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question:
What is the value of

(1.001 times 1.001 times 1.001+0.999 times 0.999 times 0.999)/(1.001 times 1.001-1.001 times 0.999+0.999 times 0.999) ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the expression as the **algebraic identity** (a³ + b³) ÷ (a² − ab + b²).

The simplified form of this **identity** is always equal to (a + b).

Here, let a = 1.001 and b = 0.999.

Required **Value** = 1.001 + 0.999 = 2.000.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 1.001

b = 0.999

**Formula Used:**

The **sum of cubes** identity is given by: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expression = (1.001 × 1.001 × 1.001 + 0.999 × 0.999 × 0.999) ÷ (1.001 × 1.001 − 1.001 × 0.999 + 0.999 × 0.999)

⇒ Expression = (1.001³ + 0.999³) ÷ (1.001² − 1.001 × 0.999 + 0.999²)

⇒ Expression = [(1.001 + 0.999) × (1.001² − 1.001 × 0.999 + 0.999²)] ÷ (1.001² − 1.001 × 0.999 + 0.999²)

⇒ Expression = 1.001 + 0.999

⇒ Expression = 2.000

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference of Cubes Identity

The formula for the difference of two cubes is a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Difference of Squares

The identity for the difference of two squares is a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

Square of a Binomial

The expanded form of (a + b)² is a² + 2ab + b² and for (a − b)² is a² − 2ab + b².</p

questions.question: What is the least five-digit number that is exactly divisible by 21, 35, and 56?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of the given numbers 21, 35, and 56, which is 840.

The smallest **five-digit number** is 10000.

Divide 10000 by 840 to find the remainder: 10000 ÷ 840 ⇒ **Remainder = 760**.

The least multiple of 840 above 10000 is 10000 + (840 − 760) = 10080.

**∴ The correct answer is 10080.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors = 21, 35, and 56. Target = **Least five-digit number**.

**Formula Used:** Required number = Smallest n-digit number + (LCM − Remainder of Smallest n-digit number / LCM).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7978b1489a0fb19702bebf38dccf6a7756a41b23be3892e84944446a3e442198.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 21 = 3 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 35 = 5 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7 = 2³ × 7

⇒ **LCM** = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7 = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840

⇒ Smallest five-digit number = 10000

⇒ 10000 ÷ 840 ⇒ Quotient = 11, Remainder = 760

⇒ Required number = 10000 + (840 − 760)

⇒ Required number = 10000 + 80 = 10080

**∴ The correct answer is 10080.**

**__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by taking the highest power of all prime factors involved.

Greatest n-digit Number Divisible by X

To find the greatest n-digit number divisible by a set of numbers, divide the largest n-digit number (e.g., 99999) by their **LCM** and subtract the remainder.

Divisibility Rule for 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8. For 10080, 080 is divisible by 8.</p

questions.question: After increasing the selling price of an article by 25%, the new price of the article becomes Rs. 250 . Now a discount of 25% is offered on the new price. What would be the profit or loss in percentage on the original price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When any value is first increased by R% and then decreased by R%, there is always a net loss.

The net loss percentage is given directly by the formula: Loss % = (R² ÷ 100)%

Here, R = 25%. (The absolute value of Rs. 250 is not needed for finding the percentage).

⇒ Net Loss % = (25² ÷ 100)% = 625 ÷ 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price after a 25% increase = Rs. 250

Discount offered on the new price = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Original Price − Final Selling Price

Loss Percentage = (Loss ÷ Original Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/421951bbfbc4e14677dcdf1f54a64e88596ada9a2668ce73cf14a8d10ca2a7f9.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the original price of the article be x.

⇒ x + 25% of x = 250

⇒ 1.25x = 250

⇒ x = 250 ÷ 1.25 = Rs. 200

Now, a 25% discount is offered on the new price (Rs. 250).

⇒ Discount = 25% of 250 = (25 ÷ 100) × 250 = Rs. 62.5

⇒ Final Selling Price = 250 − 62.5 = Rs. 187.5

Since the Final Selling Price is less than the Original Price, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = Original Price − Final Selling Price

⇒ Loss = 200 − 187.5 = Rs. 12.5

⇒ Loss Percentage = (12.5 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. If it's an increase, use a positive sign; if a decrease, use a negative sign.

Same Increase and Decrease

If a number is increased by R% and then decreased by R%, the net effect is always a decrease (or loss). The effective loss is calculated as (R² ÷ 100)%.

Extraneous Data in Percentage Problems

In questions asking strictly for a final percentage or ratio, the absolute numerical values (like Rs. 250) are not required and can be safely ignored to save calculation time.
</p

questions.question: A thief escapes from a police station at 8:00 a.m. on a cycle at a speed of 50 km/h. A policeman starts chasing the thief on a motorbike at 9:30 a.m. at the speed of 65 km/h. At what distance from the police station will the policeman catch up with the thief?

A policeman starts chasing the thief on a motorbike at 9:30 a.m. at the speed of 65 km/h.

Concept used:

1. Time taken to meet for two objects coming towards each other = Intermediary distance ÷ Relative speed

2. Relative speed is the difference between individual speeds while two objects run in the same direction.

3. Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Time difference = 9:30 a.m. - 8:00 a.m. = 1.5 hours

Distance between the thief and the policeman when the policeman starts chasing

⇒ 1.5 × 50 = 75 km

So, the time taken to catch up = frac {75}{65 - 50} = 5 hours

Now, the distance from the police station the will policeman catch up with the thief

__
 
• The national income in India is calculated by the** ****National Statistical Office.**
 
• The NSO was formed by merging the CSO and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) to streamline statistical activities in India.

• **Product Method- **

• **Income Method-**
 
• In this method, a total of net income earned by working people in different sectors and commercial enterprises is obtained. By this method, NI is obtained by adding receipts as total rent, total wages, total interest, and total profit.
 
• **Consumption Method-**
 
• It is also called the expenditure method.
 
• Income is either spent on consumption or saving. Hence, National Income is the addition of total consumption and total saving.

__
 
• In the reflex action, the reflex arch is formed by Receptor → Spinal cord → Muscle.
 
• The correct circuit of the reflex arc is Receptor→sensory neuron→spinal cord→motor neuron→effector
 
• A **reflex arc is a neural pathway that controls a reflex action. In vertebrates, instead of passing directly to the brain, the sensory neuron's synapse in the spinal cord.
 
• This helps in a faster reflex action** without the delay that is caused by routing signals through the brain.
 
• The three main types of neurons are sensory, motor and relay neurons.

The **detailed process is**

 
• The receptor detects a stimulus.
 
• Sensory neurons send electrical impulses to a relay neuron located in the spinal cord.
 
• Relay neurons connect sensory neurons to motor neurons.
 
• Motor neurons send an electrical impulse to an effector.
 
• Effector produces a response.

questions.question: The quartzite is a _______ type of rock.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metamorphic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**

 
 
• These rocks form under the action of volume, pressure, and temperature (PVT) changes.
 
• **Metamorphism happens when rocks are forced down to lower levels by tectonic processes or when molten magma rising through the crust comes in contact with the crustal rocks or the underlying rocks are exposed to great amounts of pressure by overlying rocks.**
 
• The materials of rocks chemically modify and recrystallize due to thermal metamorphism.
 
• There are two types of thermal metamorphism: **Contact metamorphism and Regional metamorphism.**
 
• Contact metamorphism: The rocks come in contact with hot intruding magma and lava and the rock materials recrystallize under high temperatures.
 
• Regional metamorphism: The rocks experience recrystallization due to deformation caused by tectonic shearing together with high temperature or pressure or both.
 
• **Quartzite is a metamorphic rock. Hence, Option 4 is correct.**
 
 
• The original form of Quartzite is pure quartz **sandstone. **
 
• It is formed when quartz-rich sandstone is exposed to high temperatures and pressures.
 
• Quartzite is mainly formed through two types of metamorphism namely** Contact and Barrovian.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Rocks**

 Igneous rocks
 
 
Formed due to the cooling, solidification, and crystallization of magma. 

 
The common examples of igneous rocks are basalt, gabbro, etc.

 
 
 

 Sedimentary rocks 
 
 
Formed due to the accumulation or deposition of sediments derived from the older rocks, plants, and animals. 

 
The common examples of sedimentary rocks are sandstone, conglomerate, etc.

 
 
 

 **Metamorphic rock **
 They are formed when existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure, or reactive fluids, such as hot, **mineral-laden water. For example, Marble, Quartzite, Schist, etc.**

questions.question: Which international day was observed for the first time on 12 April 2025, as declared by the United Nations?

options.text: International Day of Human Space Flight
International Day for Dialogue Between Civilizations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Day of Human Space Flight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day of Human Space Flight** is observed annually on **12 April** to commemorate the first human space flight.
 
• This day marks the anniversary of the first manned space mission by **Yuri Gagarin**, a Soviet cosmonaut, on **12 April 1961**. This historic event made Yuri Gagarin the first human to travel into outer space.
 
• The United Nations General Assembly declared the observance of this day on **7 April 2011**, through a resolution to recognize the beginning of the space era for humanity.
 
• The day celebrates **human achievements in space exploration** and promotes international cooperation for peaceful uses of outer space.
 
• Yuri Gagarin’s spacecraft, **Vostok 1**, completed one orbit around the Earth in **108 minutes**, a milestone in the history of space exploration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of Human Space Flight:**

 
 
• The space era began with the launch of the first artificial satellite, **Sputnik 1**, by the Soviet Union on **4 October 1957**.
 
• Yuri Gagarin’s historic flight on **12 April 1961** made him an international hero and demonstrated the potential for human space exploration.
 
• His spacecraft, **Vostok 1**, traveled at a speed of around **27,400 km/h**, reaching an altitude of 327 kilometers.
 
• This achievement paved the way for subsequent human space missions, including the **Apollo Moon landings** and the establishment of the **International Space Station (ISS)**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of International Day of Human Space Flight:**
 
 
• The day highlights the significance of **space technology** and its contributions to scientific research, innovation, and global development.
 
• It promotes the peaceful use of outer space and encourages international cooperation in space exploration.
 
• The observance inspires new generations to pursue careers in **science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM)** fields.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Observances:**
 
 
• **World Space Week:** Celebrated annually from **4 to 10 October**, it highlights the benefits of space exploration.
 
• **Moon Day:** Observed on **20 July**, it commemorates the first human Moon landing by Apollo 11 in 1969.
 
 
 
• **Space Exploration Milestones:**
 
 
• **1969:** Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon during NASA’s Apollo 11 mission.
 
• **2001:** Dennis Tito became the first space tourist.
 
• **2021:** The first civilian spaceflight was launched by SpaceX under the Inspiration4 mission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Yuri Gagarin:** He was a Russian pilot and cosmonaut who became the first human to journey into outer space. His flight lasted **108 minutes**.
 
• **Vostok 1:** This spacecraft carried Yuri Gagarin into space. It was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in present-day **Kazakhstan**.
 
• The **United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA)** plays a significant role in promoting international cooperation in space exploration.
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** is an example of global collaboration in space research, involving countries like the USA, Russia, Japan, Canada, and European nations.
 
• The advent of private companies like **SpaceX, Blue Origin,** and **Virgin Galactic** has further revolutionized space travel and exploration.
